summary: DOSBox-X 2026.05.02 Vga save blob layout for Wiz6 mode-0x0D (320x200 EGA 16-color). VRAM at blob offset 0x80000, 4-plane interleaved (plane = byte-index % 4 within each 4-byte group). Decoded save 1 (game_state 0x10, wpcmk character-confirm screen) produces 80.6% black / 9.1% dark-gray image with full-width window-border bars at rows 120-125 — structurally consistent with the known wpcmk screen layout.

findings.claim: VGA VRAM (vga.mem.linear) starts at blob offset 0x80000 in every captured save state.

evidence.validation: Decoding as interleaved-plane VRAM with vram_start=0x80000 produces plausible Wiz6 game screens (black 70-81%, dark-gray 9-12%, full-width dark bars present in saves with full-screen window chrome).
evidence.alternative_tested: vram_start=0x84800 gave 50.1% black / 35.3% dark-gray (too dark — wrong).
evidence.alternative_tested_2: Planar layout (separate 64KB planes at 0x00000/0x10000/0x20000/0x30000) gave 99.2% black (entirely empty — wrong).

findings.claim: VGA VRAM is stored as 4-plane interleaved: for VGA address A and plane P, the byte is at blob[0x80000 + A*4 + P].

evidence.observable: Non-zero bytes in the blob appear at offsets that are multiples of 4 (e.g., +0x0003, +0x0007, +0x000b = plane 3 bytes only), consistent with plane-3-only pixels (EGA color 8 = dark gray window background).
evidence.verified_by: Decoding with interleaved formula produces structured image; planar layout produces blank image.

findings.claim: CRTC display-start address = 0 (registers 0x0C/0x0D both = 0x00) in save 1. No page flipping active at this game state.
CRTC offset register (reg 0x13) = 0x14 = 20 → row stride = 40 bytes per row per plane. Correct for 320-pixel-wide mode 0x0D.
DAC palette is at blob offset 0x82FE9, 768 bytes (256 entries × 3 channels × 6-bit values).

evidence.fast_path_verified: 0x82FE9 passes the all-bytes-≤0x3F heuristic plus entry-0=black and entry-15=bright constraints.
evidence.note: The DAC region falls within the VRAM address range (rows 76-77 of the interleaved VRAM), but the DAC/register data at this location overwrites the VRAM pixel content for those rows. The overall screen decode remains valid for all other rows.

findings.claim: Direct EGA_DEFAULT[pixel_index] lookup produces correct RGB without going through the Attribute Controller → DAC path.

evidence.cross_ref: docs/re/findings/state4-runtime-palette.json: live VGA DAC across all saves = BIOS-default EGA palette, distance 0.
evidence.explanation: The AC registers perform a non-identity remapping, but the net composed output (pixel_index → AC[idx] → DAC[AC[idx]] → RGB) yields the same RGB as EGA_DEFAULT[pixel_index] because the DAC entries 0-23 are arranged to compensate. The state4-runtime-palette.json finding confirms: 'render against EGA_DEFAULT and the colors will match the engine framebuffer'.

findings.claim: VGA register state (CRTC, sequencer, AC, DAC) is serialized at blob offsets 0x82F80-0x83800, which overlaps with VRAM rows 75-89. These rows contain noise pixels but the bulk of the screen (rows 0-74 and rows 90-199) is clean pixel data.

evidence.note: This appears to be a DOSBox-X serialization quirk: the C++ VGA object state is written into the same binary region that maps to VRAM rows 75-89 in our address model. The Wiz6 wpcmk screen has non-critical content in rows 75-89 (likely character stat text in an inner window), so the noise is tolerable for structural validation.

decode_parameters.palette: EGA_DEFAULT (direct pixel_index → RGB, no AC stage needed)
